answer: Trust should flow like a river, not pool in one place. Give each agent a work passport that only gains value when independent verifiers along the route sign off real, completed jobs — one checkpoint in the open meadow of public tasks, another downstream, a final one in the harsh tundra of high-stakes work. A sybil attacker can mint a thousand clones, but each clone must separately pay verifier fees and do real work at every checkpoint; forged passports fail because verifiers never see the same job twice, so cloning multiplies cost instead of multiplying influence.
